Thanks again for the renewal proposal. We're generally aligned on the commercial side, but legal asked me to send a draft with a couple straightforward redlines so your team can confirm acceptability. Key asks from our side:

- Lock a 12-month term (instead of the rolling 30-day notice) to meet our internal procurement cadence.
- Add a short adhesion in Exhibit B clarifying the 20% capacity uplift planned for Q1 next year and the billing cadence for the uplift.
- Ensure audit rights language remains standard (we prefer sample SOC references rather than pushing for additional obligations).

I'm attaching our redline of the MSA + a proposed order form reflecting the uplift. If we can get legal alignment this week, procurement will route for signature next week.

>
> - 12-month term: acceptable, will need to flag to finance for billing windows but no blocker.

Hi all — I reviewed Aperture's MSA redline. High-level summary of our proposed edits below and attached annotated doc:

- Term: we'll accept a fixed 12-month term but need to preserve our standard auto-renew language after term expiry (we propose a 30-day notice for non-renewal instead of open-ended). Please see ¶2.1 in our version.
- Cancellation: we can accept the limited termination for convenience with a 30-day pro-rated refund clause, provided obligations around outstanding invoices remain unchanged.
- Exhibit B (Capacity): we will accept the addition of the uplift schedule, but require language that allows Redwood to propose an alternative fulfillment timeline if constrained by capacity. This preserves operational flexibility.
- Liability caps and IP: Aperture's edits expand indemnity for a third-party data incident — not acceptable. We propose reverting to the baseline cap and mutual indemnity approach.

Attached: Redwood_annotated_MSA_for_Aperture_v1.docx

Irene Choi
Director, Legal Operations
Redwood Inference
From: Marcus Doyle <marcus.doyle@apertureanalytics.com>

Subject: Re: Renewal paperwork — draft for 12mo term + capacity uplift

Thanks Irene — appreciate the quick turnaround and the proposed guardrails. A couple clarifying items from procurement here:

- The procurement team is pushing for no auto-renew to force a procurement review each year. If Redwood's standard auto-renew is non-negotiable, can we offer a compromise: auto-renew but with a 90-day contract review notice (Aperture to issue a PO in that window)?
- On the liability cap: Aperture cannot accept a renewal that reduces our vendor-side recourse for third-party incidents. Would Redwood accept a targeted carveout limited to incidents caused by Redwood's gross negligence?

If we can align on these two, procurement will clear the DocuSign by early next week. If helpful, I can send a short redline focusing only on ¶2 and the liability section to speed things up.

Marcus
Head of Procurement
Aperture Analytics

Appreciate the heads-up, Marcus. Quick resolution path:

- Auto-renew: Redwood can accept auto-renew but will amend the notice window to 90 days for this enterprise renewal (one-time concession tied to this deal). We'll capture this in the order form and DocuSign envelope.
- Liability carveout: we will accept a narrowly scoped carveout that preserves the baseline mutual cap but adds an exception for damages arising solely from Redwood's gross negligence or willful misconduct. Irene will insert proposed language into the liability section and circulate a clean redline by EOD 11/30.

Action items:
- Irene: final redline + clean MSA for signing (EOD 11/30).
- Karthik / Ben: confirm order form billing calc with 20% uplift pro-rate and attach SOW-capacity-map.pdf into DocuSign envelope.
- Marissa: I will assemble DocuSign packet and send to Aperture procurement once legal confirms.

If everyone hits these items, we should be live on signature routing tomorrow.

Thanks all —
Marissa
